purpose: Research baseline, not a parity or release certification
coverage: Initial language families plus complete headings from pinned ledger ADT and standard library API references. Not exhaustive semantic-case coverage.

baseline.qualification: Latest stable release and network matrix differ. Network qualification of 0.36.1 is not established by matrix.

evidenceKinds.SEM: Positive and negative source/type/evaluator cases against pinned documented semantics and independent expected values.
evidenceKinds.ZK: Native lowering plus official checker/prover/verifier, including adversarial witness/public-input cases.
evidenceKinds.LEDGER: Isolated ledger finalized acceptance/rejection, exact state/events, atomicity and transaction binding.
evidenceKinds.ABI: Canonical byte/value representation, bounds, argument/result schema and artifact metadata fixtures.
evidenceKinds.HOST: Same portable artifact and vectors in at least two independent host-language runners.
evidenceKinds.PROVENANCE: Pinned source/tool versions, hashes, build/dependency closure and reproducible artifact manifest.

statusMeaning.missing: No corresponding supported frontend/native route found in inspected Nightlean source.
statusMeaning.subset: Some corresponding implementation exists, not full Compact feature equivalence.
statusMeaning.related-subset: Related example/primitive exists, semantic equivalence to named Compact API unverified.

features.notes: Bool values, equality, constants and constraints exist. General Boolean operators and Compact conversion semantics are absent.
Native canonical field literals, add and mul exist. Subtraction, full conversions and mixed Uint arithmetic are absent.

Pinned compiler uses inclusive maxima internally. For ordinary Uint<0..m> and Uint<0..n>, addition returns exclusive bound m+n-1 and multiplication returns (m-1)*(n-1)+1. This contradicts the looser reference prose. Subtraction retains the left maximum and asserts a nonnegative result. Follow pinned implementation parity, not prose equations. Nominal aliases have separate checked-result rules.

sourceDerivedRules.appliesTo: Ordinary Uint operands and structural aliases, excluding nominal numeric aliases
sourceDerivedRules.maximumGuard: result inclusive maximum <= 2^248 - 1, checked before nominal result downcast
sourceDerivedRules.literalTyping: Literal v has minimal prefix range [0,v], not a singleton-refined type
sourceDerivedRules.declaredBinding: Declared const/parameter type controls later variable-reference inference
sourceDerivedRules.condense: Unwraps structural aliases and records nominal identities without shifting bounds
sourceDerivedRules.constantOptimization: Parameter cases do not depend on folding. expand-const splits declarations, and arithmetic inference precedes circuit simplification
sourceDerivedRules.nominalAliases: Same nominal identity and underlying type required. Result keeps original nominal type, with checked downcast when maximum grows

conformanceCases.input: Parameter x: Uint<8>, expression x+0; repeat with parameter z: Uint<0..1>
Parameter x: Uint<8>, typed const z: Uint<8> = 0, expression x+z
conformanceCases.expected: Maximum 510. Returning as Uint<8> rejects without a cast.

conformanceCases.input: Parameters x: Uint<248>, b: Uint<1>, expression x*b
Parameters x: Uint<248>, z: Uint<0..1>, expression x+z
Parameters x: Uint<248>, b: Uint<1>, expression x+b
conformanceCases.expected: Maximum 2^248. Rejected by arithmetic inference before result annotation.

conformanceCases.input: Two parameters of a structural Uint<8> alias
conformanceCases.expected: Same maxima and assignment decisions as ordinary Uint<8> operands.

conformanceCases.input: Two parameters of one nominal Uint<8> alias
conformanceCases.expected: Result retains alias. 255+1 fails downcast, 1+1 succeeds. Different nominal identities reject statically.

features.notes: Byte literals, padding, conversion, canonical encoding and length bounds.
Fixed-size homogeneous arrays, indexing, slicing, spread and bounds.
Heterogeneous tuples, vector subtyping, destructuring, access, spread and unit returns.
Named fields, defaults, construction, access, destructuring, spread and generic structs.
Member creation, comparisons, bounds, casts and defaults.

Structural Uint aliases use inclusive-maximum widening. Nominal numeric aliases require matching identities, retain their original type and downcast checked arithmetic results. The max-unsigned guard precedes nominal downcasting. See C-LANG-UINT conformance cases.
Host-only values and restrictions on circuit usage/serialization must be explicit.

Compare normalized inclusive Uint maxima. Source/prose result-bound discrepancy changes return, binding, ledger-write and argument acceptance. See C-LANG-UINT conformance cases. Compact value semantics need a Lean surface design rather than copied syntax.
Each permitted and rejected source/target pair, range failures, byte order and foreign-field restrictions.
Defaults for every supported type, including inactive Maybe/Either payloads.
select evaluates both arms in Nightlean. This does not establish Compact branch/short-circuit equivalence.
Guard witness calls, failed assertions, state effects and event effects correctly.
Range endpoints constant or nat parameters, or fixed-size vectors/tuples/bytes. Return within loop rejected.
Do not confuse expression map with ledger Map.
Parameters, arity, results, helper calls and recursive-call rejection.
Pure circuits exclude ledger operations, events and witness calls.
Specialization and invalid/recursive instantiation cases.
Namespace and visibility behavior, top-level exports, generic modules.
const binding, shadowing, destructuring and left-to-right expression evaluation.
Equivalent explicit Nightlean compatibility target, without Compact syntax or toolchain dependency.
Boolean constraints exist. Failure attribution and unit-valued assertions need equivalence cases.
Current explicit input visibility supports a fixed claim. No full exported-argument disclosure policy.
General call signatures, context, private-state return, ordering and failure behavior need host-neutral ABI.
State ownership, persistence and failure/commit boundaries are host responsibilities with shared semantics.
Track private values through data/control flow, outputs, ledger writes, events, cross-calls and declassifying commitments.
Native runtime config initializes scalar cells and explicitly empty maps. No general constructor language or witness initialization.
Reject mutations reachable from exported circuits, including helper calls.
Map value nesting and typed ledger paths need explicit layout and operation semantics.
Non-generic provable signatures. Pure interface circuits rejected in 0.36.x.
Bind address, entry-point hash, arguments/results and communication commitment. Enforce conformance, key agreement, no re-entry, witness restrictions.
Only standard event types, ordered VersionedLogItem v1 encoding. Constructor emission rejected. General custom event declarations are not assumed.
Native .zkir/key generation and one local ledger claim proven. Latest 0.36.1 reference bundles ZKIR 3.2.1, local POC used 3.2.0.

features.surface: Contract metadata, manifests and source provenance
features.notes: Native plan/profile hashes and receipts exist. Full exported-type/interface ABI, manifest and artifact validation contract is absent.
Node ESM evaluator exists for Native/Bool and symbolic Impact plan. No second-language implementation or full canonical ABI.
One native private claim finalized with exact state match. Multi-call, checkpoints, coins, all ADTs and malicious transcript variations unqualified.
Source spans, type/capability errors exist. Need stable error categories and negative corpus, not identical Compact wording.
Exposed by ledger SDK, not a Compact language primitive. Include deployment lifecycle tests as a separate compatibility track.

features.surface: Wallet, funding, proof, deployment and indexer integration
features.notes: Isolated localnet deployment/funding exists for claim. SDK replacement is outside language parity, portable adapters still need qualification.
Native primitive and claim proved. No inference of equivalence to generic transientHash, Merkle leaf hashing or Compact serialization.
